entries.title: DRAFT: a bounded first Poisson moment permits an atom
entries.statement: For the positive probability measure mu=delta_0 and P_eta(E)=eta/(E^2+eta^2), integral_R P_eta(E)dE=pi for every eta>0 although mu is purely atomic; integral_R P_eta(E)^2 dE=pi/(2 eta). A uniform first energy moment does not imply absolute continuity.
entries.proof_text:
## L1: first moments do not exclude atoms

For mu=delta_0 its unnormalised Poisson transform is P_eta(E)=eta/(E^2+eta^2). Direct substitution gives integral_R P_eta=pi and integral_R P_eta^2=pi/(2 eta). Thus a bounded first energy moment is consistent with a purely atomic measure. The second equality exhibits the obstruction at heights tending to zero. This example concerns a scalar spectral measure and is not a counterexample to the lattice conjecture.
assumptions: eta>0
P_eta is the unnormalised Poisson transform of mu=delta_0

entries.title: DRAFT: an annealed density can conceal atomic sample measures
entries.statement: If S is Uniform[-1,1] and H_S is the scalar self-adjoint operator S, its sample spectral measure is mu_S=delta_S, but E mu_S has density (1/2)1_[-1,1]. For every real E and eta>0, E Im(S-E-i eta)^(-1)<=pi/2. Thus uniform expected first resolvent imaginary parts do not imply samplewise absolute continuity.
entries.proof_text:
## L2: an annealed density can conceal purely atomic sample measures

Let S be Uniform[-1,1], let H_S be multiplication by S on a one-dimensional Hilbert space, and let mu_S=delta_S. Each sample spectral measure is atomic, but E mu_S has density (1/2)1_[-1,1]. For every E and eta>0,

E Im(S-E-i eta)^(-1)=(1/2) integral_[-1,1] eta/((s-E)^2+eta^2) ds <= pi/2.

This follows by extending a nonnegative integral to R. A uniform bound on the expected scalar imaginary part therefore cannot be promoted to samplewise absolute continuity. Conditioning on the other variables does not alter this one-dimensional counterexample.
assumptions: S is Uniform[-1,1]
H_S acts on a one-dimensional Hilbert space
E is real and eta>0

entries.title: DRAFT: higher Poisson moments imply almost-sure absolute continuity
entries.statement: Let mu_omega be random positive Borel measures on R of mass at most one, I a bounded open interval, p>1, and eta_n a deterministic positive sequence decreasing to zero. Put P_omega,eta(E)=integral eta/((t-E)^2+eta^2)dmu_omega(t). If sup_n E integral_I P_omega,eta_n(E)^p dE<=C<infinity, then almost surely mu_omega restricted to I has an Lp density f_omega, and E integral_I |f_omega(E)|^p dE<=C/pi^p.
entries.proof_text:
## L3: a higher Poisson moment is sufficient

Let mu_omega be random positive Borel measures of mass at most one, let I be a bounded open interval, and let p>1. Define P_omega,eta(E)=integral eta/((t-E)^2+eta^2) dmu_omega(t). Assume for a fixed deterministic sequence eta_n decreasing to zero that

sup_n E integral_I P_omega,eta_n(E)^p dE <= C < infinity.

Then almost surely mu_omega restricted to I has an Lp density f_omega, and E integral_I |f_omega|^p <= C/pi^p.

Proof. Put X_n=integral_I P_eta_n^p. Fatou gives E liminf_n X_n<=C, hence liminf X_n is finite almost surely. For such a sample, choose a subsequence along which X_n tends to its finite lower limit. Boundedness in reflexive Lp(I) gives a weakly convergent further subsequence, with limit h. For each phi in C_c(I), extend phi by zero to R. The normalised Poisson convolution of phi converges uniformly to phi. Fubini, and the bound on total measure, therefore give lim integral_I phi P_eta_n=pi integral phi dmu. Weak convergence identifies h dE=pi dmu on I. This proves absolute continuity on the whole open interval, not merely on a prescribed full-Lebesgue-measure subset. Weak lower semicontinuity gives pi^p ||f||_p^p<=liminf X_n. Fatou yields the expected norm bound. The density and its norm are measurable; for example, approximate identities give a jointly measurable representative and the norm bound also follows from a countable dense family of continuous tests. The hypothesis is on a genuine pth moment, not the pth power of an expectation.
assumptions: random positive Borel measures with measurable integrals and mass at most one
I is bounded and open
eta_n decreases deterministically to zero
uniform expected pth energy moment is finite

entries.title: DRAFT: inverse cavity-width moments give quenched spectral absolute continuity
entries.statement: Let H be bounded self-adjoint on l2(Z^3), with bounded deterministic hopping and iid real site variables of bounded support and bounded probability density rho, scaled by a fixed lambda>0. Delete x to obtain H^x and its hopping vector b_x, and put Gamma_x(E,eta)=eta+Im<b_x,(H^x-E-i eta)^(-1)b_x>. Fix 0<q<1 and an open interval I. If for each x and each compact interval J contained in I, sup_{0<eta<1} E integral_J Gamma_x(E,eta)^(-q)dE<infinity, then almost surely all site spectral measures restricted to I are absolutely continuous, with locally L^(1+q) densities, and chi_I(H)l2(Z^3) is contained in the absolutely continuous subspace. This is a conditional criterion; the moment bound is not established for the lattice Anderson model here. Nonzero spectral weight is a separate requirement.
entries.proof_text:
## L4: conditional cavity negative moments supply L3

Let H be a bounded self-adjoint lattice Hamiltonian with bounded deterministic hopping, iid real site variables V_x of probability density rho in L-infinity(R), and diagonal lambda V_x with lambda>0 fixed. Bounded support is sufficient for boundedness and is imposed here. Delete site x to obtain the compression H^x. Write b_x for its hopping vector and

M_x(z)=z+<b_x,(H^x-z)^(-1)b_x>,
Gamma_x(E,eta)=Im M_x(E+i eta)>0.

For p=1+q with 0<q<1, the Schur complement and own-site independence give

G_xx(z)=(lambda V_x-M_x(z))^(-1),
E[(Im G_xx(E+i eta))^p | {V_y:y!=x}]
<= (||rho||_infinity/lambda) c_p Gamma_x(E,eta)^(1-p),
c_p=integral_R (1+u^2)^(-p)du=sqrt(pi) Gamma(p-1/2)/Gamma(p).

Proof. Freeze the complement so that M_x=a+i gamma is fixed and gamma>0. Integrate [gamma/((lambda v-a)^2+gamma^2)]^p against rho(v)dv, bound rho by its supremum, extend to all real v, and substitute u=(lambda v-a)/gamma. The result is exactly the displayed upper bound. This proof uses independence of the own-site variable from the full complement, not independence of different neighbours.

Consequently, if for every x and every compact interval J contained in I there is C_x,J<infinity such that

sup_{0<eta<1} E integral_J Gamma_x(E,eta)^(-q)dE <= C_x,J,

then almost surely every basis spectral measure is absolutely continuous on I, locally with L^(1+q) density. To prove it, apply the conditional inequality, Tonelli, and L3 to J's interior along eta_n=1/(n+1). Countably many intervals with rational endpoints exhaust I. Countably many sites give one event on which all site measures are absolutely continuous on I. If B is a null Borel subset of I then <delta_x,chi_B(H)delta_x>=0 for all x, so chi_B(H)delta_x=0 for every basis vector and chi_B(H)=0. This is precisely pure absolute continuity of the spectral restriction. This conclusion by itself permits the projection on I to vanish; nonzero mass must be established separately.

The hypothesis is an unproved sufficient condition for the lattice model, not a theorem asserting that the lattice satisfies it. It is stronger than the qualitative cavity-boundary-positivity route used in recent primary literature. No necessity is asserted.
assumptions: bounded self-adjoint H on the countable lattice
bounded deterministic hopping
bounded-support iid site law with rho in L-infinity
fixed lambda>0
own-site variable independent of the entire complement
uniform inverse cavity-width energy moment on each compact interval J contained in I

entries.title: DRAFT: bounded-potential perturbation stops at positive height
entries.statement: For the six-neighbour lattice, H_lambda^x=H_0^x+lambda V^x with ||V^x||<=1, lambda>0 and z=E+i eta with eta>0, ||(H_lambda^x-z)^(-1)-(H_0^x-z)^(-1)||<=lambda/eta^2. With ||b_x||^2=6, the corresponding cavity escape widths differ by at most 6 lambda/eta^2. A free lower bound Gamma_0,x>=c>0 yields Gamma_lambda,x>=c/2 by this estimate only under the sufficient restriction eta^2>=12 lambda/c. This estimate supplies no uniform control as eta tends to zero at fixed positive lambda.
entries.proof_text:
## L5: the bounded-potential perturbation route stops at positive height

Take the six-neighbour lattice and ||V||_infinity<=1. Let H_lambda^x=H_0^x+lambda V^x. At z=E+i eta the resolvent identity and ||(H_lambda^x-z)^(-1)||<=1/eta give

||R_lambda^x(z)-R_0^x(z)||<=lambda/eta^2,
|Gamma_lambda,x(E,eta)-Gamma_0,x(E,eta)|<=6 lambda/eta^2.

The factor six is ||b_x||^2. If a free lower bound Gamma_0,x>=c>0 holds on an energy set and at the heights under consideration, this proves Gamma_lambda,x>=c/2 only when eta^2>=12 lambda/c. For a fixed positive lambda it leaves a whole interval of arbitrarily small heights uncontrolled. It cannot prove L4's supremum over all heights. The displayed restriction is sufficient, not a claimed necessary bound or a physical transition scale.
assumptions: six-neighbour deterministic hopping of magnitude one
bounded site potential of norm at most one
lambda>0 and eta>0
the lower-bound consequence additionally assumes Gamma_0,x>=c>0

entries.title: DRAFT: rejected first-moment route to sample spectral absolute continuity
entries.statement: Rejected inference: a uniform first energy moment of a scalar Poisson transform, or a bounded density of the disorder-averaged spectral measure, implies almost-sure absolute continuity of the sample measures. This implication is false: delta_0 and the random scalar operator with uniform eigenvalue give exact counterexamples. A higher moment or another argument excluding sample singular mass is required.

entries.title: DRAFT OPEN GAP: inverse cavity-width moments on the cyclic cubic lattice
entries.statement: Proposed sufficient-condition research target, not an established theorem: for H=-A+lambda V on l2(Z^3), V_x iid Uniform[-1,1], find q in (0,1), lambda_0>0 and a deterministic nonempty bounded open interval I of nonzero spectral weight such that for each fixed 0<lambda<lambda_0, each site x and each compact interval J contained in I, sup_{0<eta<1} E integral_J [eta+Im<b_x,(H^x-E-i eta)^(-1)b_x>]^(-q)dE<infinity. H^x is the compression deleting x and b_x has the six hopping coefficients. This bound would supply a conditional spectral route; it would not prove GOE microscopic statistics. No proof of this bound is supplied.

relations.rationale: Own-site conditioning yields the higher Poisson moment to which the pathwise Lp compactness criterion is applied.
The atom has uniformly bounded first Poisson energy moment but is singular.
An absolutely continuous expected spectral measure coexists with purely atomic measures in every sample.
The conditional theorem identifies exactly the still-unproved lattice hypothesis required by this route.
The deterministic perturbation estimate loses its lower bound as eta tends to zero and does not close the gap.
Uses Lp reflexivity with 1<p<infinity on the finite Lebesgue interval; excludes the p=1 endpoint.
The Poisson approximate-identity representation is compatible with inversion; the returned pointwise density clause already assumes absolute continuity and is not used to prove it.
Continues the recorded closed-recursion and fixed-coupling limit obstruction without reusing a spanning-tree transfer.
